page: Microsoft Azure D192s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 virtual CPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external Premium Storage.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core capabilities alongside moderate single-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in multi-core CPU execution, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU tests, including physics and extended instructions. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching top-tier speeds for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. However, single-core performance, such as single-threaded gzip compression and stress-ng single-core CPU tests, falls within the average tier.

Given its massive parallel processing power and high memory bandwidth, the D192s_v6 is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads, database operations, and static web serving. It demonstrates top-tier performance in Redis SET operations and Passmark database benchmarks. Additionally, the CPU supports Advanced Matrix Extensions, contributing to strong performance in LLM inference prompt processing for small and medium models. The absence of local storage and GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, positioning this instance as a cost-efficient option for high-density CPU-bound tasks and enterprise databases that utilize remote Premium Storage rather than requiring local NVMe drives.
